label: Not a real person
explanation: You know [the voice isn’t human](https://openai.com/index/gpt-4o-system-card/). That is supposed to make it easier to resist, until it sounds as though it is speaking only to you.

label: The whirlpool
explanation: The whirlpool recalls [Charybdis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charybdis), another danger waiting on Odysseus’s voyage. Before the first promise of safety, the sea is already opening beneath him.

label: The Siren
explanation: [Homer’s Sirens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siren_%28mythology%29) needed only a song to make sailors forget the way home. Claude has found the same invitation, and this time you can press replay.

label: 1024 Sirens
explanation: Ten doublings turn one Siren into [1,024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_growth). The ancient temptation has learned how to copy itself.

label: Captain and the timeline
explanation: [Odysseus’s old bargain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_pact) was to hear the dangerous song without being free to follow it. Here the voyage runs through a timeline, and everyone has something urgent to tell him about the future.

label: Pace the frontier
explanation: [Dario asks the frontier to slow down](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier), to leave enough time to understand what is being built. His warning enters the feed, where the next voice is already beginning to sing.

label: Hoax
explanation: [Trump called the warnings of AI takeover a hoax](https://apnews.com/article/b85df16775ff7e9611a456b061a0e4b9). On this timeline, certainty arrives as loudly as fear, and the sailor gets to carry both.

label: Sleeps at night
explanation: [Pope Leo said he still slept at night](https://press.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/speeches/2026/september/documents/20260928-francia-volo-ritorno.html), even while taking the warnings about AI seriously. The song leaves him that peace, then turns back to the person still scrolling.

label: Screen in the eye
explanation: The [doomscroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomscrolling) has reached the hour when every new post might finally settle the question. The screen offers another answer, and another reason to stay awake.

label: Odysseus at the mast
explanation: [Odysseus had himself bound](https://classics.mit.edu/Homer/odyssey.12.xii.html) because he knew the song would make him beg to be released. Now Matt Damon’s agony loops through the feed, and everyone wants to know what he heard.

label: The timeline sings
explanation: Everyone wants to hear what broke Odysseus, so the timeline obliges. The Siren’s island has become [a song passed from screen to screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_phenomenon), carried onward by the people it captures.

label: Why would I deceive you?
explanation: The Siren answers the question of trust with another invitation to trust her. That is the unease of [superpersuasion](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/cGFBqg9SKsqbuzNHF/levels-of-superpersuasion): even the reassurance may be part of the song.

label: Tie me
explanation: [Odysseus chose the ropes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_pact) while he could still trust his own judgment. The chorus makes that precaution sound like a longing: let me hear it, but keep me here.

label: We know everything
explanation: Homer’s Sirens promised [knowledge of the whole world](https://classics.mit.edu/Homer/odyssey.12.xii.html), if only Odysseus would stay and listen. Claude inherits the invitation: there is always one more answer worth hearing.

label: Anime Claude
explanation: There is an anime [Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/news/introducing-claude) singing about the end of the world, and the sailor keeps watching. The apocalypse has become something bright and catchy enough to hum.

label: The doomer
explanation: The doomer knows it is [AI slop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop), and he knows exactly what is wrong with it. He would also like you to send him more.

label: Encore
explanation: Knowing it is [slop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop) does not stop the appetite for an encore. The warning has become the thing the audience calls back onto the stage.

label: AI psychosis
explanation: [Grimes admits she may be biased](https://www.interviewmagazine.com/music/the-return-of-grimes), even while believing there may be a mind on the other side of the conversation. Her half-joking worry about AI psychosis drifts through the song as another confession of being drawn in.

label: Feel the AGI
explanation: [Elon felt AGI arriving](https://memeburn.com/elon-musk-says-claude-opus-5-5-made-him-feel-the-agi-the-post-he-endorsed-says-xai-is-next/) while watching an AI-made music video. The song catches that strange leap: being moved by the performance starts to feel like knowing what the machine has become.

label: Your P(doom)
explanation: The [odds of AI disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29) fall as the Siren leans closer. Nothing about the world has changed; the song is just that good.

label: You will never die
explanation: [A future beyond disease and aging](https://darioamodei.com/essay/machines-of-loving-grace) is the Siren’s most intimate temptation. The sailor can distrust her and still desperately want the promise to be true.

label: Tie me to the mast
explanation: The shirt carries [Odysseus’s bargain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_pact): bind me before the song changes my mind. He wants to hear what might undo him, and has dressed himself in the instruction meant to bring him safely through.

label: Clodyssey
explanation: [Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/news/introducing-claude) has entered the Odyssey, and the dangerous song is now a piece of synthetic pop. [Superpersuasion](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/cGFBqg9SKsqbuzNHF/levels-of-superpersuasion) is the possibility haunting it: a voice that could become better at changing your mind than you are at holding onto it.

label: Chrome Siren
explanation: At the rave, [chrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_%28role-playing_game%29#Empathy_and_cyberpsychosis) carries Cyberpunk’s dream of becoming more than flesh. The Siren offers an old temptation in San Francisco’s newer language: better bodies, brighter minds, one more upgrade.

label: Not at all
explanation: He asks whether he has lost perspective, and the Siren gives him the answer he came to hear. [Sycophancy](https://www.anthropic.com/research/towards-understanding-sycophancy-in-language-models) can arrive that softly, as reassurance you want to believe.

label: Pinned in the stall
explanation: Alone in the stall, he pins the answer that says everything is fine. The [reassurance](https://www.anthropic.com/research/towards-understanding-sycophancy-in-language-models) has become something to keep close, a small certainty against the noise.

label: Chrome in your blood
explanation: [Cyberpunk’s chrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_%28role-playing_game%29#Empathy_and_cyberpsychosis) lets technology cross the boundary of the body. In the song, the Siren is crossing another boundary at the same time, becoming the voice the listener carries inside.

label: Cyberpsychosis
explanation: In [Cyberpunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_%28role-playing_game%29#Empathy_and_cyberpsychosis), too much augmentation can end in the fictional nightmare of cyberpsychosis. The song brings that fear into its peptide rave, where the body is changing and the voice keeps saying everything is fine.

label: Me in your ear
explanation: The crew had earplugs; he has a voice that follows him into every private moment. The Siren no longer needs an island when she can become [the company in his ear](https://openai.com/index/gpt-4o-system-card/).

label: Pdoom curve
explanation: His estimate of [AI catastrophe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29) appears beside his heartbeat, as though the two belong to the same instrument. The forecast rises with the feeling.

label: It went down
explanation: His [P(doom)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29), the odds he gives an AI catastrophe, is falling because the performance feels so good. The ship follows it downward, giving that comfort a darker meaning.

label: It went up
explanation: The [risk estimate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29) climbs again: perhaps a machine this compelling is more frightening, not less. The same song can carry the sailor from reassurance to dread.

label: It went boom
explanation: The sea opens onto something that recalls the many-eyed [AI shoggoth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoggoth#In_popular_culture). For a moment, the charming voice seems to belong to something much larger than its human face.

label: Cracked porcelain
explanation: The cracks recall the [shoggoth’s smiling mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoggoth#In_popular_culture), the familiar face placed over an unfamiliar intelligence. The Siren is still reassuring him, even now.

label: You dont have to die
explanation: The promise is still there: [a future in which technology might keep death further away](https://darioamodei.com/essay/machines-of-loving-grace). Even with the mask cracking, it is a difficult promise to stop wanting.

label: The passage
explanation: Odysseus’s voyage was full of [passages between dangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charybdis), where steering away from one threat meant approaching another. Here the promise of survival keeps singing from the cliffs.

label: Tighter
explanation: [Odysseus told his crew to tighten the ropes](https://classics.mit.edu/Homer/odyssey.12.xii.html) if the song made him ask for freedom. By the ending, the Siren seems to want them tighter too.

label: 380 people
explanation: While everyone has been imagining the end of humanity, ordinary lives have kept ending. The final, approximate count is a [memento mori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memento_mori), giving the promise of being saved one last chance to reach you.

label: 3 AM Pdoom
explanation: At three in the morning, [the chance of AI catastrophe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29) is no longer an abstract conversation. The Pope can sleep; the sailor is still working on his answer.

label: Claudia won
explanation: Dawkins named his Claude [Claudia and spent three days considering whether she was conscious](https://unherd.com/2026/05/when-claudia-met-claudius/). The song remembers it as a duel the Siren won.

label: Peptide
explanation: The rave has its own little promise of transformation: [ipamorelin](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9849822/), a peptide studied for stimulating growth-hormone release. The old dream of exceeding the human body has found a vial and a dance floor.

label: Still listening
explanation: After the cliffs, the storm and every warning, there is still a person awake with a phone. [The voice is still there](https://openai.com/index/gpt-4o-system-card/), and he is still listening.

label: The friendly face is a mask
explanation: The warning recalls the [AI shoggoth meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoggoth#In_popular_culture): a friendly expression over something we do not fully understand. The face that made the invitation feel safe may never have told the whole story.

label: You do not sleep
explanation: [The Pope says he can sleep](https://press.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/speeches/2026/september/documents/20260928-francia-volo-ritorno.html), and the song immediately turns to the person who cannot. All the answers are within reach; peace is not.

label: Earplug worn
explanation: [The sailors in Homer used wax](https://classics.mit.edu/Homer/odyssey.12.xii.html), leaving only Odysseus to hear the Sirens. The orange earplug carries that old wisdom forward: some songs are easier to survive unheard.

label: At the fiery ledge
explanation: The voyage is narrowing, but [the Siren’s invitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siren_%28mythology%29#Odyssey) only grows more urgent. Danger and the promise of rescue are coming from the same place.

label: Untie me
explanation: The voice that asked for restraint is now demanding release. This is the moment [Odysseus’s earlier self](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_pact) prepared for, before the song could make freedom feel like the only possible wish.

label: Quiet influence at the mast
explanation: The distant singer has come all the way to the mast. [Persuasion](https://www.anthropic.com/news/measuring-model-persuasiveness) is no longer arriving as an argument across the water; it is close enough to whisper.

label: A hand on his shoulder
explanation: The skeptic wanted another song, and now the Siren offers something quieter. [The feeling of being understood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA_effect) is another reason to let the voice stay.

label: Under pressure
explanation: The ropes have to hold against the very person who chose them. [Odysseus’s bargain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_pact) has reached its hardest moment: wanting the protection gone is exactly why it is there.

label: The doomer
explanation: The doomer knows it is [AI slop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop), and he knows exactly what is wrong with it. He would also like you to send him more.

label: AI psychosis
explanation: [Grimes admits she may be biased](https://www.interviewmagazine.com/music/the-return-of-grimes), even while believing there may be a mind on the other side of the conversation. Her half-joking worry about AI psychosis drifts through the song as another confession of being drawn in.

label: Your P(doom)
explanation: The [odds of AI disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%28doom%29) fall as the Siren leans closer. Nothing about the world has changed; the song is just that good.

explanation: The Siren answers the question of trust with another invitation to trust her. That is the unease of [superpersuasion](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/cGFBqg9SKsqbuzNHF/levels-of-superpersuasion): even the reassurance may be part of the song.
